title: Writing in Egyptian: messages, wishes and condolences

blocks.text: While ARZ units teach you to read the written dialect, this unity teaches you to write it: a message to a friend, an invitation, a voice message, and above all formulas for occasions (birthdays, marriages, births, outdated examinations, diseases, mourning, religious holidays), which in Egypt are almost mandatory and always have a fixed response. Wronging a formula is not serious, but knowing them well is a sign of respect that Egyptians notice and appreciate. You will also learn to choose the log (Egyptian or fuṣḥā simple) according to the recipient. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-12INT-04INT-05, the Test B2.2 and the beginning of B2-13.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 202–210), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, an Arabic keyboard on your phone or computer
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. write in Arabic characters a clear and consistent Egyptian message in the graphs;
2. use formulas for happy occasions and their answers;
3. tactfully write a message of closeness for an illness or mourning;
4. choose between Egyptian and fuṣḥā simple according to the recipient and the situation;
5. record and understand a voice message in Egyptian.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
210 Active recall review Unit verification

Voice messages in Egypt ( ⁧فويس⁩ · voice) are often more frequent than written ones, even among colleagues. A good voice message: begins with a greeting and the name; state the reason immediately; not more than one minute; closes with a formula (sallim li..., mistanni raddak). Understand a vowel. It is spontaneous spoken: breaks, laughter, noises, changes of theme. The method: 1) listen to everything to understand who, why and what he asks you; 2) listens and records dates, times, places; 3) answer in writing by taking the data (ʿašān atʾakkid: il-ḥadd is-sāʿa Sit down, ṣaḥḥ?).
